                // Dense vector\n    std::vector<double> h_out(numRows);                 // Output vector\n\n    printf(\"Initializing data structures...\\n\");\n    fill(h_vec.data(), numRows, maxVal);\n    fill(h_val.data(), nItems, maxVal);\n    initRandomMatrix(h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(), nItems, numRows);\n\n    // For validation, compute reference solution\n    std::vector<double> h_reference;\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Computing reference solution...\\n\");\n        h_reference.resize(numRows);\n        spmvCpu(h_val.data(), h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(), \n                h_vec.data(), numRows, h_reference.data());\n    }\n\n    // Perform SpMV computation\n    printf(\"Computing SpMV...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    for (index_t iter = 0; iter < iterations; ++iter) {\n        spmvCpu(h_val.data(), h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(),\n                h_vec.data(), numRows, h_out.data());\n    }\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate performance metrics\n    const double gflops = (2.0 * nItems * iterations) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    const double avgTime = duration.count() / static_cast<double>(iterations);\n    \n    printf(\"Average time per iteration: %.3f ms\\n\", avgTime);\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(h_out, \"OutputVector\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        const bool valid = verifyResults(h_reference.data(), h_out.data(), numRows);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n256","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}}

s=s.replace(old2,new2)\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncmake --build /tmp/spmv_build 2>&1 | grep -E \"warning|error|Built\"; B=/tmp/spmv_build/spmv\nfor n in 1024 4096 16384; do echo \"--- n=$n default threads\"; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011Cg6VH5KmNY2nwC7o4bdgZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01C1pEsBmsx5qoZ9z4NiXnB5","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'\np='spmv.cpp'; s=open(p).read()\ns=s.replace('#include <omp.h>\\n','#include <omp.h>\\n\\n#ifdef __linux__\\n#include <sched.h>\\n#endif\\n',1)\nold='''    // Spin up the OpenMP thread pool once so that team creation is not charged\n    // to the first timed iteration.\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        // Intentionally empty: warm up the thread pool.\n    }\n'''\nnew='''    // Spin up the OpenMP thread pool once so that team creation is not charged\n    // to the first timed iteration, and pin the pool threads to CPUs.\n    warmUpAndPinThreads();\n'''\nassert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)\nold2='''void printUsage(const char* progName) {'''\nnew2='''// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: warmUpAndPinThreads\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Creates the OpenMP thread pool and pins each pool thread to a distinct CPU\n//   from the process' allowed CPU set. Unpinned threads migrate between cores\n//   and sockets, which destroys cache locality and NUMA affinity for the\n//   memory-bound SpMV kernel. Pinning is skipped if the user has already\n//   requested binding via OMP_PROC_BIND / OMP_PLACES, or if the OpenMP runtime\n//   cannot report the binding policy.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid warmUpAndPinThreads() {\n#ifdef __linux__\n    const bool pin = (omp_get_proc_bind() == omp_proc_bind_false);\n    std::vector<int> allowedCpus;\n    if (pin) {\n        cpu_set_t mask;\n        CPU_ZERO(&mask);\n        if (sched_getaffinity(0, sizeof(mask), &mask) == 0) {\n            for (int c = 0; c < CPU_SETSIZE; ++c) {\n                if (CPU_ISSET(c, &mask)) {\n                    allowedCpus.push_back(c);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n#pragma omp parallel default(none) shared(allowedCpus)\n    {\n        if (!allowedCpus.empty()) {\n            const int tid = omp_get_thread_num();\n            const int cpu = allowedCpus[static_cast<size_t>(tid) % allowedCpus.size()];\n            cpu_set_t mask;\n            CPU_ZERO(&mask);\n            CPU_SET(cpu, &mask);\n            sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(mask), &mask);\n        }\n    }\n#else\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        // Intentionally empty: warm up the thread pool.\n    }\n#endif\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {'''\nassert old2 in s; s=s.replace(old2,new2)\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncmake --build /tmp/spmv_build 2>&1 | grep -E \"warning|error|Built\"; B=/tmp/spmv_build/spmv; uptime\nfor n in 1024 4096 16384 32768; do echo \"--- n=$n default (256 threads, self-pinned)\"; Only the two existing files changed, the executable is still `spmv`, and the build has no warnings.\n\n**What changed in `spmv/spmv.cpp`**\n\n- **Kernel parallelized.** The row loop in `spmvCpu` runs under `omp parallel for schedule(static)`. Rows are independent and the matrix structure is uniform, so a static split is well balanced and keeps each thread's slice cache-resident across iterations. The per-row summation order is untouched, so output is bit-identical to the serial code.\n- **Team sizing.** The team is capped so each thread owns at least 8192 non-zeros. Without this, a 256-thread fork on the default 1024-row matrix cost more than the work itself.\n- **Thread pinning.** The thread pool is created once before the timed loop and each thread is pinned to a distinct CPU from the process's allowed set via the POSIX scheduler API. Unpinned threads on this 2-socket SMT machine ran 6 to 8 times slower. Pinning is skipped if the user already set OMP_PROC_BIND, and the code falls back to a plain warm-up on non-Linux.\n- **NUMA-aware first touch.** The value and column arrays use a no-initialization allocator and are first-touched in parallel with the same static partition the kernel uses. The sequential random fill then writes into already-placed pages. The output vector stays a plain `std::vector<double>` because `print_results` requires it.\n\nMatrix generation and `fill` stay serial since they consume `rand()` sequentially and must produce the identical matrix.\n\n**`spmv/CMakeLists.txt`** adds `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`, so OpenMP is always on.\n\n**Verification.** Validation passes at every size and thread count tested, and the `-r` result hash is identical between 1 thread and 256 threads.
